design_rules.student_simplicity: The learner will eventually see guided journeys, Review, and Challenge Lab; F2 classification machinery remains hidden.
design_rules.locus_rule: A permanent locus represents one coherent causal, spatial, or comparison model rather than one canonical record.
design_rules.embedded_rule: Related definitions, mechanism details, and teacher enrichment are embedded in the locus whose scientific action makes them intelligible.
design_rules.practice_rule: Applied-transfer records remain in Challenge Lab and do not consume permanent palace locations.
design_rules.scope_guard_rule: Scope guards protect AP boundaries and remain non-runtime support metadata unless a later audit needs to surface them.
design_rules.process_rule: Photosynthesis and respiration must preserve scientifically recognizable membrane, compartment, redox, gradient, and pathway geometry.
design_rules.narrative_gate: No polished Unit 3 story prose may be authored until F3 scene briefs pass QA.
design_rules.spelling_rule: No mandatory spelling gate. Exact-name support is adaptive and can use optional sound cues only when useful.

journeys.content_focus: Catalysts, activation energy, active-site compatibility, induced fit, and enzyme reuse
journeys.setting_logic: A molecular workshop makes the reaction barrier, docking geometry, and catalytic turnover visible before terminology is attached.

journeys.content_focus: Environmental effects, enzyme concentration variables, helpers, inhibition, allostery, cooperativity, and pathway regulation
journeys.setting_logic: A control wing allows one enzyme system to be stressed, supplied, blocked, activated, and regulated while preserving clear distinctions among mechanisms.

journeys.content_focus: Metabolism, thermodynamics, free energy, cellular work, ATP structure, coupling, and regeneration
journeys.setting_logic: An energy-accounting hall keeps forms of energy, thermodynamic constraints, work, and ATP cycling inside one causal system instead of treating them as separate definitions.

journeys.content_focus: Photosynthetic origins, chloroplast geography, light, pigments, photosystems, electron transport, proton gradients, and photophosphorylation
journeys.setting_logic: A light-processing conservatory follows energy from incoming photons through pigments, photosystems, electron transfer, proton-gradient formation, ATP, and NADPH.

bundles.title: Linear electron flow and energy products

journeys.content_focus: Calvin cycle, carbon fixation, Rubisco, RuBP, G3P, photorespiration, C4, and CAM
journeys.setting_logic: A carbon greenhouse turns ATP and NADPH into visible carbon-flow work, then tests how plants reduce photorespiration under different environmental constraints.

journeys.content_focus: Aerobic respiration from fuel intake through glycolysis, mitochondrial oxidation, electron transport, proton gradients, ATP synthase, heat, and prokaryotic respiration
journeys.setting_logic: A power plant follows carbon and electrons through successive energy-harvesting stages while keeping mitochondrial compartments and chemiosmosis spatially explicit.

journeys.content_focus: Aerobic versus anaerobic respiration, fermentation, NAD+ recycling, alcohol fermentation, and lactate metabolism
journeys.setting_logic: A branching annex compares alternative routes from shared metabolic constraints so anaerobic respiration and fermentation cannot collapse into the same idea.
